premises.text: Seniors forget to engage walker brakes before sitting, causing fall injuries
premises.evidence_span: even though her physiotherapists tell her constantly to always engage the brakes before sitting on the walker, she sometimes forget

premises.text: Steep hills and ramps make walkers unstable and cause walk-related fall injuries
premises.evidence_span: These steep hills and ramps can cause instability when seniors try to descend it, and thus lead to a walk-related fall injury

premises.text: A sensor-equipped smart walker perceives user intention and environment and actuates brakes to reduce injury risk
premises.evidence_span: capable of perceiving user intention, the environment around us, and actuating appropriately to minimize the risk of injuries

premises.text: Licensing the technology to walker manufacturers for factory integration is the go-to-market path
premises.evidence_span: our go-to-market strategy is to take this technology, license it to walker manufacturers

value.text: Safeguard seniors from walker-related falls and raise quality of life
value.evidence_span: These features safeguard seniors from falls, leading them to a higher quality of life

secondary_value.evidence_span: help seniors reduce fall-related injuries, alleviate healthcare expenses

causal_links.evidence_span: these are problems that seniors face today

notes: Singleton D2/D3 retained: sensing-actuation and OEM licensing are separately revisable. Sensor list (pressure, encoders, accelerometers) folded into P3 per §4.1(5). Host intro and user-video speech excluded per §4.2. Market-size figures excluded as framing/traction.
